Subject: TeleHealth RFI — model risk & governance detail request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for confirming intake. TeleHealth Group is running an RFI for vendors who will support inference on PHI-adjacent clinical workflows. Procurement asked us to gather detailed responses around model risk, governance alignment (NIST AI RMF), and EU AI Act positioning for our regional customers.

Top asks (we can accept a short packet but need clear artifacts):
- NIST AI RMF mapping: how you identify, assess, and monitor risks across phases (inception -> deployment -> monitoring)
- EU AI Act classification/positioning and whether Redwood supports the specific mitigation controls (transparency, human oversight, logging, data residency)
- Eval/regression approach: how you prevent quality regressions when swapping models or updates (prompt sets, automated eval harness, acceptance criteria)
- Evidence: sample playbook, test harness overview, SOC/Security artifacts, redaction/data handling docs
- Timeline: can you provide a response packet by Aug 6?

We are especially interested in examples relevant to telemedicine (short clinical summaries, triage prompts). Please let me know if you need a template.

Best,
Sara Lin
Director, Clinical Integrations
TeleHealth Group

Sara / Kimberly —

Quick technical notes to supplement Kim's packet:

- Eval harness: we run evaluations in two parallel lanes — a regression lane (existing production prompts and canonical answers) and a scenario lane (simulated clinical flows). Both are automated in our CI with runbooks.
- Acceptance criteria: we surface metric thresholds (ROUGE/BERTScore for free-text where applicable, plus domain-specific classifiers for triage correctness). We also include human-in-the-loop audits on sampling intervals (default 1% of production queries or 1k queries/day, whichever larger).
- Canary & rollout: staged rollout with traffic shifting + shadow testing. Canary failsafe triggers auto-revert based on weighted metrics (latency SLA breach, degradation in accuracy delta).
- Data handling: for hosted customers we anonymize and use KV prefix caching; for PHI use-cases we recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS and region pinning.

I attached an expanded NIST->Feature mapping CSV and a short script snippet we use to compute regression deltas. Happy to walk through via technical call.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara / Team —

Adding a short ML operations note for the RFI packet:

- Regression sets: we maintain both synthetic and seeded anonymized real prompts categorized by sensitivity level (triage, diagnosis summary, recommendation). For telehealth we recommend a dedicated "clinical triage" prompt set maintained in a private repo with version pins.
- Model variants & quantization: we benchmark full-precision and quantized candidates against the regression set; acceptance requires parity within defined deltas on the primary clinical metric and no material increase in hallucination rate measured by our classifier.
- Explainability & human oversight: for high-risk flows we surface provenance metadata (prompt fingerprint, model version, KV cache state) in logs, and provide an optional UI for clinicians to mark outputs for retraining.
- Monitoring signals: drift (embedding drift), latency tail, token-level hallucination signal, and user override rate. Alerts tied to automated rollback.

I'll include a short snippet that shows our regression runbook steps in the final packet.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
